title: The Arch Old Knight Of York

contact_edits.before: The staging (Glenn Casale) and sets (John Iacovelli) are very makeshift. Rachel York has charm and spunk as Guenevere, while showing again that it's impossible to play this role without sounding exactly like Julie Andrews, not only in the range and colour of her singing, but in the roguishness of her speech. That said, her singing of Before I Gaze at You Again, not previously a song to which I've ever paid much attention, is the evening's high point. An actor with the unlikely name of Time Winters gets all the available fun out of King Pellinore, a transplanted English clubman who arrives at court in search of the Questing Beast, like (he says) all the Pellinores before him, and then forgets about it for the rest of the show. He's fortunate, for purely technological reasons, in not having to sing. We have suffered much recently from overbearing sound systems; now here's one that's underbearing. It makes everyone, from the vibrant Ms. York to the modest Mr. York, sound as if their vocal cords have been wrapped in cotton wool. - Camelot runs until June 30. For more information call 416-872-2262.
